reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. grep for data-visibility in b.css returns nothing; the only rules that read it are in render-b.js (lines 324, 353, 373). Driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-editing and pressing Hidden: data-visibility flips shown->hidden, .b-grabWord flips Shown->Hidden, and nothing else moves - item opacity stays 1, .b-title computed colour stays rgb(255,255,255) at weight 400, tick unchanged. Same drive in ?v=paper: title stays rgb(17,17,17), opacity 1. So a moment guests will never see is drawn at exactly the ink of one they will, and the entire signal is one 11px uppercase mono word at --fore-62. The gate assertion at interaction-check.mjs:522 is indeed named 'the row follows the toggle in ink and in words' but readVis() (lines 503-513) reads only the attribute, the chip text, the aria-label and aria-pressed - it never samples a computed colour, so the ink half of its own claim is unenforced. The undo half is also true and worse than stated: visButton's click handler (render-b.js:400-409) only rewrites aria-pressed and calls setVisibility; it never touches history, and after the toggle .b-undo still reads data-empty="true". A one-day date nudge is reversible; hiding a moment from the couple's families is not. Real, specific, and the highest-stakes irreversibility on the screen. The FIX as written is not safe and must not be applied verbatim - see sharpenedFix: --fore-46 fails AA on the paper ground, and the .b-tick clause is a no-op that becomes a defect.
sharpenedFix:
Keep the diagnosis, replace the three CSS clauses and tighten the JS.

1) NOT --fore-46 on the title. Measured against the real composited backdrop: --fore-46 is 4.65:1 on the ink ground (passes) but 3.11:1 on the paper ground (rgba(17,17,17,0.46) over #ffffff = rgb(146,146,146)). .b-title is 17px/400 at phone and tablet widths (the 24px large-text step only applies under [data-medium="sheet"|"full"]), so 3.11:1 is a normal-text AA failure - and ?v=paper is a shipped room and state=print force-sets ground=paper (render-b.js:792). The same applies harder to the proposed .b-away/.b-date clause: those are 15px and 11px, never large text. Use --fore-62 instead: 7.67:1 on ink, 5.33:1 on paper, AA on both, and still an unmistakable density drop from --fore. So: .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-title { color: var(--fore-62); font-weight: 400; } and, if the count must recede with it, .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-away { color: var(--fore-62); } (down from --fore-72). Leave .b-date alone - it is already --fore-62 and cannot go lower without failing AA on paper. Note the font-weight:400 clause deliberately strips the 600 from a hidden lead or anchor row; that is correct (a moment guests cannot see should not be the boldest thing on the measure) but it is a second signal, so state it rather than let it happen by accident.

2) DROP the .b-tick clause as written. It is factually wrong about the rail: every non-lead tick is ALREADY an outline ring - b.css:151-159 gives .b-tick border:1px solid var(--fore-46) with background:var(--back) - so 'outline against a filled one' is a no-op for all but the lead item. Worse, background:transparent is an active regression: measured at 1440, .b-rail sits at x=710 and the tick spans x=707-714, so the tick's --back fill is what knocks the rail out from behind it. Make it transparent and a 1px rule strikes through the middle of every hidden dot. Mark hidden on the rail by keeping the knockout and changing the ring instead: .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-tick { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--fore-46); background: var(--back); } and, so the one filled accent mark is never spent on a moment guests cannot see, .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"][data-lead="true"] .b-tick { background: var(--back); border-color: var(--fore-46); width: 7px; height: 7px; left: -23px; top: 6px; } (that selector must sit after the [data-lead] block, which has equal specificity).

3) The history push needs more than one line. paintUndo (render-b.js:283-309) unconditionally computes Math.abs(top.to - top.from) and emits 'moved N days', and undo() (481-490) unconditionally calls setAway and focuses a .b-step - a visibility record pushed into that array prints 'moved NaN days' and restores the wrong thing. So: give every record a kind (tag the existing date push kind:"date" too), branch paintUndo on it ('Last change: ' + title + ' hidden from guests.' / ' shown to guests.'), and branch undo() to call setVisibility(item, last.from) AND re-sync the segmented control's aria-pressed on both .b-seg buttons if the editor is still open - otherwise undo leaves the toggle claiming a state the row no longer has, which is the exact drift the setAway comment says round 1 was fixed to prevent. Focus after a visibility undo should land on the pressed .b-seg button, not a .b-step.

4) Extend the gate as proposed, but assert the composited contrast too, not just difference: in interaction-check.mjs readVis(), capture getComputedStyle(title).color and fontWeight, require the hidden value to differ from the shown value, and require the undo bar's data-empty to go to "false" after the toggle. Then re-run audit.mjs on ?v=paper and state=print to prove the new hidden-row colours still clear AA on the paper ground.
